methodology_gaps: OAuth2 callbackUrl open redirect not directly tested — profiling identified the parameter but did not probe ?callbackUrl= with external domains to confirm/refute redirect validation
NextAuth.js CSRF endpoint /api/auth/csrf not probed — CSRF token entropy and session fixation behavior untested
Backend CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin value not retrieved — CORS policy permissiveness unknown despite CORS headers being observed
No rate limiting check on /api/auth/* endpoints — brute-force and credential stuffing exposure unknown
Pusher channel authorization endpoint not enumerated — backend route /pusher/auth or equivalent not probed for unauthenticated access
pay.copointdata.com and accelerate.copointdata.com HTTP responses not captured — timed out in profiling, leaving high-value subdomains uncharacterized
revops.copointdata.com (production) not deeply profiled — only existence confirmed; security header posture, auth config, and endpoint differences vs dev not compared
/api/csp-report POST endpoint not tested for injection or abuse potential
No JavaScript source map or bundle enumeration — /_next/static/ JS bundles not fetched for API route discovery or secrets in client-side code
v0.dev-generated UI components not identified individually — AI-generated components may contain unsanitized inputs; no component-level recon performed
Backend /health response does not disclose version string — version enumeration via other routes (/, /version, /api) not attempted

lessons.text: NextAuth.js deployments always expose /api/auth/providers unauthenticated by design — immediately enumerate all provider callback URLs as OAuth redirect attack surfaces in wave 1 auth testing
When backend hostname is exposed via CSP connect-src, enumerate beyond /health — probe /api, /v1, /v2, /docs, /swagger, /openapi.json unauthenticated before assuming full auth protection

Azure Container Apps environment names in hostnames (livelystone) can be used to enumerate sibling apps — other containers in the same environment may share the livelystone-c1480484.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io namespace

Dev environment returning env:production from /health is a misconfiguration signal — dev and prod may share the same backend container image/config, meaning dev environment has full production data access

Pusher WebSocket integrations require a backend channel authorization endpoint — probe /pusher/auth, /api/pusher/auth, and /realtime/auth before any authenticated session is obtained to check unauthenticated channel subscription
Payment subdomain (pay.copointdata.com) resolved but timed out — dedicated subdomain takeover and tech-stack fingerprinting wave needed before payment-specific auth and data access testing

Next.js /_next/static/ JS bundles contain client-side route definitions, API paths, and occasionally leaked secrets — always enumerate and fetch main chunks for API surface mapping before auth testing

CSP nonces observed to rotate per-request on /login — XSS via script injection is blocked at the CSP layer; focus XSS testing on DOM-based sinks and non-script injection vectors (iframe, meta refresh, object)

CORS headers present on backend but Access-Control-Allow-Origin not captured — always capture CORS preflight response in wave 1 to determine if credentials-bearing cross-origin requests are allowed from arbitrary origins
v0.dev AI-generated UIs tend to implement client-side validation only — prioritize server-side input validation testing on all form fields and API parameters in post-auth waves
